holidays.name: National Whipped Cream Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the fluffy, sweet cloud that improves pies, cocoa, sundaes and the occasional spoonful straight from the can. Swirl it, dollop it or spray it. Just don't skimp.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a fixture on the food-holiday calendar, and it arrives right after the holiday season's peak dessert days.
holidays.funFact: Whipped cream is made by trapping tiny air bubbles in fat droplets from cream. The cream needs at least about 30% butterfat to hold its shape well.

holidays.name: National Bird Day
holidays.description: A day to look up and appreciate our feathered neighbors, from backyard sparrows to soaring eagles. It also encourages people to think about bird conservation and the welfare of pet birds.
holidays.origin: National Bird Day was started in the early 2000s by bird-welfare advocates. They chose January 5 to bring attention to threats facing wild and captive birds, and the date comes just after the winter bird-count season begins.
holidays.funFact: Birds are living descendants of dinosaurs, so your local pigeon is technically a distant cousin of T. rex.

holidays.name: National Keto Day
holidays.description: A New Year's resolution holiday for people who love the low-carb, high-fat way of eating. It's a day to try bacon-and-avocado creations and cauliflower versions of just about everything.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It appeared as people started setting health goals for the new year.
holidays.funFact: The ketogenic diet was developed in the 1920s as a medical treatment for epilepsy, long before it became a popular weight-loss trend.
